subject: Inference ramp & latency margins for JunoAI deal
messages:
From: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@juno.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@juno.ai, Taylor Wu <taylor.wu@juno.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inference footprint & ramp model for Juno deal

Hey Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start drafting the SOW we need a realistic estimate of the committed capacity and how fast we can ramp safely without violating our 99th/95th latency targets. High-level ask:

- Baseline profile: 200k requests/day, avg 120 tokens/request, but with spikes up to 12x (internal events).
- Target latency: 95th <= 180ms, 99th <= 300ms for standard chat flows.
- Need a conservative ramp plan and a canary plan for first 30 days.

I attached the initial traffic profile from our telemetry — it has per-minute spike windows and payload size percentiles. Would appreciate a first-pass tokens/sec and GPU mapping we can put in the procurement packet. Also, any thoughts on quantization or model variants that preserve QA for our use case would help.

Attachments: juno_initial_traffic_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Cheers,
Alex Rivers
Head of Platform
JunoAI
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@juno.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference footprint & ramp model for Juno deal

Alex —

Got the profile, thanks. Looping Ben and Karthik to surface an operational plan and rough GPU sizing. First impressions: your peak-minute pattern (12x) and the 120 token avg points to a wide instantaneous tokens/sec range; we should plan for a combination of reserved pool + short burst capacity.

Next steps: Ben will drop a tokens/sec -> GPU mapping and a few latency tradeoffs. Karthik will note runtime knobs (prefix cache, KV warmup, quantized model options) that can reduce needed GPUs without hurting 95/99 tails.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to align on the canary window and acceptance metrics? Prefer 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@juno.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference footprint & ramp model for Juno deal

Alex / team —

I ran a quick pass with the traffic profile. Key numbers (first-pass, conservative):

- Avg tokens/sec (sustained): ~3500 tokens/sec (this is across the 24h window using avg requests).
- Peak tokens/sec (1-min spike at 12x): ~42,000 tokens/sec.
- Steady 95th quantile token/sec (common spikes): ~9,000 tokens/sec.

Model choice: if you use a 8-bit quantized open model (we tested a fine-tuned 7B variant for similar workloads) the per-GPU sustainable tokens/sec (A100 80GB-ish equivalent) is ~11k tokens/sec for interactive chat with KV caching; H100 gives ~18k tokens/sec in our config.

Initial mapping (conservative):
- Reserved pool (commit): 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs -> ~72k sustained tokens/sec capacity (this covers expected steady and moderate spikes with 20% headroom).
- Short burst buffer (on-demand): scale to an extra 4-6 H100s for minute-level peaks.

Latency: with the above and aggressive prefix/KV caching we project:
- 95th latency: ~140-160ms
- 99th latency: ~260-320ms (depends on tail evictions and network egress).

Notes / risks:
- If Juno wants hard 99th <= 250ms we recommend either higher reserved GPUs (6 H100s) or a hybrid with a slightly smaller model (faster per-token) for tails.
- Quantization helps but some hallucination/regression risk needs to be covered in evals.

I've attached a short estimate sheet. Ben

Attachments: juno_estimates_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@juno.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@juno.ai, Taylor Wu <taylor.wu@juno.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference footprint & ramp model for Juno deal

Ben —

Appreciate the numbers, that helps a lot. Clarifying Qs:
1) For the 4 H100 reserved pool you listed ~72k sustained tokens/sec. How much of that is usable for multi-tenant Juno flows once you account for prefix warmup (first 10 tokens of a user session) and KV cache priming?
2) Can you give a basic cost delta between 4 vs 6 reserved H100s (ballpark per month) so my procurement team has something to slot into the SOW?
3) We are firm on 95th <= 180ms and want to push 99th closer to 250ms if possible. We can tolerate some tail exceptions during the first 30 days but need a clear mitigation.

Also — we'd prefer a canary that ramps to 25% traffic on day 1, 50% day 3, 75% day 7 and full by day 14 if metrics look good. Please embed that into your operational runbook recommendation.

Thanks,
Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@juno.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference footprint & ramp model for Juno deal

Alex / team —

Quick engineering note to address the prefix/KV & canary asks. Summary recommendations:

- Effective usable capacity: expect ~10-15% transient capacity loss during cold-start windows due to KV cache warmup (first 2-5 minutes after a surge), so plan headroom for that. That means a 4 H100 reserved pool provides ~61k usable tokens/sec during cold windows.

- Canary plan (operational):
  * Day 0 (pre-canary): provision reserved 4 H100s + prepare 2 warm standby H100s for rapid scale.
  * Day 1: route 25% traffic -> monitor 95th/99th + error rates. If 99th > 300ms or error rate >0.5%, pause and increase to 6 reserved.
  * Day 3: 50% traffic -> validate tail latency (observe if 99th trending down).
  * Day 7: 75%
  * Day 14: full.

- Mitigations for tails:
  1) Deploy a tail-optimized model behind a routing rule (smaller, lower-latency model for extreme tails).
  2) Use token-budget-based shaping at the gateway to peel off long-context requests into background pipelines.
  3) Short-lived burst H100s via cloud provider for minute-level peaks.

- Cost delta (very rough): +50% monthly for 6 vs 4 H100 reserved (depends on discounting). Ben, we should produce a clear line-item for procurement.

Inline micro-estimate (conservative):
- 4 H100 reserved: baseline usable ~61k tokens/sec (cold windows), steady ~72k tokens/sec
- 6 H100 reserved: baseline usable ~92k tokens/sec
- Extra burst (4x H100) for minute peaks: covered via short-term on-demand.

I'll follow up with a one-page ops runbook snippet we can attach to the SOW.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex.rivers@juno.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@juno.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference footprint & ramp model for Juno deal

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turn. To summarize and propose next steps (so procurement has something concrete):

1) Recommended capacity (SOW line items):
   - Reserved: 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (commit) — covers steady-state and expected common spikes with ~20% steady headroom.
   - Optional uplift: reserve 6 H100s for firm 99th <= 250ms guarantee (pricing delta included).
   - Burst buffer: up to 4 additional H100s via producer burst (cloud bursts) for minute-level event peaks.

2) Canary & acceptance: 25/50/75/100% ramp over 14 days with rollback triggers on 99th latency > 300ms or error rate > 0.5%. Karthik to deliver a one-page runbook we attach to SOW.

3) Cost ask for procurement: Ben to provide a two-line monthly delta (4 vs 6 reserved) + estimated on-demand burst spend for a peak event.

4) Model / quality note: We recommend starting with a quantized 7B variant for lower per-token cost and using a tail-optimized smaller model to keep 99th in-check. Juno should run evals against their production prompts before finalizing.

Action items:
- Ben: deliver cost delta table and updated juno_estimates_v3 by EOD Monday.
- Karthik: ops runbook (one-pager) by Wednesday.
- Vivek: incorporate numbers into draft SOW and share with procurement.

Forwarding full thread below for the SOW packet.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
